meta.purpose: Turn #229's six 'static check passed but real Maya never ran' call forms into measured pass/fail rows on a real Maya 2024 session.
meta.verdict: 6/6 call forms pass on Maya 2024; the shipped pytest function tests/test_mayapy_smoke.py::test_callform_stub_disagreement_forms passes when called with real maya.cmds, and it now asserts non-default tangent types instead of Maya's default; a probe that raises after creating nodes leaves no node behind; the scene returns to its starting node count, playback range and selection.
meta.claim_boundary: Proves these six call forms work on Maya 2024 on Windows (GUI batch=False session). It does NOT prove Maya 2025/2026, and it does not prove the mayapy/standalone batch lane - mayapy cannot import maya.standalone on this box (DLL initialisation failure), so batch-only behaviour such as cmds.about(batch=True) stays unverified here. The shipped test was called as a plain function, not through pytest, so the mayapy marker and its fixtures are not exercised by this run. Values are one run per form; the shipped test is the durable check. The failure path that is measured is the driver's own deliberate probe: a mid-way failure inside the shipped test's finally block is not exercised here.

notes.kWorld_type: Maya's om2.MSpace.kWorld is a plain int; getPoint accepts it. So the stub's parameter type (MSpace) is the wrong half, not the constant: the constant is int, exactly as the stub declares.
notes.keyTangent_evidence: The probe sets linear/step, not Maya's default auto, and reads both back; a call that was silently ignored could not produce those two values.
notes.rename_clash: Maya returns a numbered name (GEO_cf253_name_holder1 here) for the second node wanting a taken name, and the node that already held it stays alive. Code must use the returned string, never the name it asked for.
notes.shipped_test_selection: Maya leaves a newly made node selected, so a probe that reads the selection after it creates its node records its own node. The driver reads the selection first, restores it after the probe, and the post-cleanup selection matches the starting one (both empty).
notes.playback_evidence: The probe sets min=2 and max=12 against a scene that starts at 1-120, so neither short flag can pass by matching a value the scene already had; both ends are asserted.
notes.cleanup_check: Cleanup is compared, not just attempted: playback range and selection are read after the restore and compared with the values the run started with, so a restore that silently put back the wrong values would be recorded as a problem.
notes.scene_state: Node count 51 before and after; playback 1.0-120.0 before and after; selection empty before and after; no GEO_cf253*/GEO_stub* node left. The instance was a fresh throwaway GUI and quit itself, so no user scene was involved at any point.
